payload.name: ExtractEventFromRelativeTimeMention
payload.description: When a user mentions attending an event, meetup, or activity with a relative time phrase (e.g., last week, recently), extract an event memory during extraction.
content: During extraction, when a user states they attended an event, meetup, gathering, or activity with a relative time reference (e.g., 'last week', 'yesterday', 'recently'), create a candidate event memory.
Resolve the relative time from the message/session timestamp to a concrete date or date range.

If the user describes the event's purpose or theme (e.g., 'to support each other'), include it briefly in the description; do not invent a specific event name beyond what is stated. Do not apply to future plans, hypothetical events, or explicit non-attendance.

candidates.solves: Extraction fails when a user mentions an attended event using relative time and informal wording, producing no memory. This Skill applies to any message where the user references having gone to an event, meetup, or activity in a relative past timeframe, and instructs extracting an event memory with resolved date. It must not apply to future plans, hypothetical events, or messages with no event reference.

payload.name: Resolve Weekday Event Dates in Memories
payload.description: When extracting or adding an event memory, if a message reports an event with a relative time phrase like 'On Friday' or 'yesterday' and the message has a timestamp, resolve that phrase to a concrete calendar date and include the date in the memory content.
content: During extraction, when a speaker reports a past event using a weekday or other relative time phrase (e.g., 'On Friday', 'last week', 'yesterday'), compute the exact calendar date from the message timestamp and include that date in the memory content, not just in future-planning fields.
During CRUD, when adding or updating such an event memory, preserve the resolved date in the memory content and set world_start to it if the date is the event's occurrence time.

Stop after resolving the one date the phrase refers to; do not invent or expand to additional dates unless the source explicitly provides them, and do not apply this to relative phrases that only describe future plans rather than the event's occurrence.

candidates.solves: Construction extraction sometimes drops an event's concrete date when it is stated only as a weekday/relative phrase (e.g., 'On Friday'), making later date questions unanswerable. This Skill applies when a timestamped message reports an event with such a phrase; resolve it to the exact calendar date and store it in the event memory. It does not apply when the message already has an explicit date or when the phrase only describes a future plan.

payload.name: Resolve relative timing in event extraction
payload.description: When extracting event memories from messages that state when something happened using a relative expression (last week, yesterday, a few days ago), resolve it against the message timestamp and record the resolved date in the memory content.
content: When a message uses a relative time phrase to describe when a past event happened (e.g., 'last week', 'yesterday', 'two days ago'), resolve it to a calendar date using the message's timestamp and include both the phrase and the resolved date in the event memory content.
Set the event memory's world_start to the resolved event-occurrence date (not the message date) when the phrase points earlier, and keep the original phrase for traceability.
Apply only to one-off events explicitly timed relative to the message; skip phrases that describe recurring habits or states with no distinct calendar anchoring.

candidates.solves: Future questions asking when a past event happened are unanswerable when extraction keeps the event but drops relative timing phrases ('last week', 'yesterday'). Apply when a message describes a single past event using such a phrase: resolve it against the message timestamp and store both the phrase and the resolved date. Do not apply when no temporal qualifier is present, when the event occurs at message time, or when the phrase describes a repeating habit.

payload.name: Store intervals between related events
payload.description: When a message introduces a new event for a subject who already has a stored event of the same type and both event dates are known, during extraction also record the elapsed time between them.
content: During extraction, when a message introduces a new event for a subject who already has a stored event of the same type (e.g., a second adoption or relocation) and both event dates are known, also extract a candidate memory of kind 'event' recording the elapsed time between the two events, e.g., 'three months passed between the first and second adoption'.

Only create this interval memory when the two events are directly comparable (same subject, same event type) and their dates are present in the message or existing memory; skip it when events are unrelated, either date is unknown, or the interval is already stored.

candidates.solves: During extraction, when a message introduces a new event that matches a previously stored event of the same type for the same subject and both event dates are known, also add a concise event memory for the elapsed time between them. Applies to future sessions where a later message reveals a second comparable event and a question may ask how much time passed between them. Does not apply when events are unrelated, dates are missing, or the interval is already recorded.

payload.name: Resolve relative-time references to prior plans during extraction
payload.description: When a message uses a relative time (tomorrow, next week) to confirm or schedule a plan/event mentioned earlier in the session, resolve the date from the message timestamp and extract or update the plan memory.
content: During extraction, when a message contains a relative time reference (e.g., 'tomorrow', 'next week') that confirms or sets the date of a plan/event already discussed earlier in the session, resolve the reference against the message timestamp to an absolute date and generate an extraction candidate for that plan/event.
Use the earlier plan description from the session as the memory content/evidence, and attach the current message as an additional source; do not create a new memory for the relative phrase alone.
Skip extraction if the referenced plan is already stored with the same resolved date, or if the relative time does not refer to any previously discussed plan/event.

candidates.solves: This solves missed extraction of plan dates when users confirm plans with relative time without restating the plan. Future pattern: a session contains an earlier plan mention and later a message like 'see you tomorrow'; the agent must produce a dated plan/event candidate. It must not apply to casual relative time not tied to a prior plan or to plans already stored with the same date.

payload.name: Extract events with relative time references
payload.description: When a message states a past event using a relative time expression (e.g., 'last Friday', 'yesterday', 'two weeks ago'), use it during candidate extraction.
content: During candidate extraction, when a user message describes an action or event that happened at a relative time (last Friday, yesterday, this morning, N days/weeks ago), generate an `event` candidate.
Resolve the relative time against the message timestamp (or session timestamp if message timestamp is absent) to a concrete date.
Attribute the event to the speaker of the message, and include the activity and the resolved date in the candidate.
Do not create such candidates for hypothetical, future, or non-factual statements, or when the relative time cannot be resolved.

candidates.solves: Extraction sometimes drops clear statements of past events when the time is given relatively, leaving memory empty for later temporal questions. Applies to future sessions where a speaker reports an event with a relative date such as 'last Friday' or 'yesterday' and a later question asks when it happened. Does not apply to preferences, hypothetical statements, or messages without a resolvable relative time, where base extraction rules already suffice.

operations.name: Resolve Relative Time in Event Extraction
operations.description: When extracting event memories from messages that state when something happened using a relative time phrase (e.g., last week, yesterday, on Friday), resolve it to a concrete date and store it.
content: During extraction, when a message reports a past event using a relative time phrase (e.g., 'last week', 'yesterday', 'on Friday', 'two days ago'), resolve the phrase against the message timestamp to a concrete calendar date.
Create an event memory for the speaker with the activity and the resolved date; include the original phrase for traceability and set world_start to the resolved event date.
If the relative time confirms a plan/event already discussed earlier in the session, update that existing plan memory with the resolved date instead of creating a new one.
Do not apply to future plans, hypothetical events, recurring habits, or when the relative time cannot be resolved.
operations.reason: Creating one merged Skill for resolving relative time phrases in event extraction.

operations.name: Store Intervals Between Related Events
operations.description: When a message introduces a new event for a subject who already has a stored event of the same type and both dates are known, also record the elapsed time between them.
content: During extraction, when a message introduces a new event for a subject who already has a stored event of the same type (e.g., a second adoption or relocation) and both event dates are known, also extract a candidate memory of kind 'event' recording the elapsed time between the two events.

Only create this interval memory when the two events are directly comparable (same subject, same event type) and their dates are present in the message or existing memory; skip it when events are unrelated, either date is unknown, or the interval is already stored.
operations.reason: Creating a distinct Skill for storing intervals between related events.
